quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! They can also hover in place by flapping their wings in a figure-eight pattern up to 80 times per second. The Pacific Northwest is home to the beautiful Rufous hummingbird, which migrates through Port Angeles each summer.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Hummingbirds
short_read.teaser: These tiny jeweled visitors to our gardens have hearts that beat over 1,200 times per minute. Discover the amazing adaptations that make hummingbirds nature's little helicopters.

medium_read.title: Hungary's Lake Balaton: The Heart of Summer
medium_read.teaser: Lake Balaton has been Hungary's favorite summer destination for generations, where families gather to swim, sail, and enjoy lakeside traditions. This beautiful freshwater lake holds centuries of Hungarian memories and culture.

long_read.title: Olympic Peninsula: Where Rainforest Meets the Sea
long_read.teaser: The Olympic Peninsula is one of the most ecologically diverse places on Earth, home to temperate rainforests, alpine peaks, and wild coastlines. Learn how this remarkable landscape right in your backyard came to be.

port_angeles.title: Dungeness Spit National Wildlife Refuge
port_angeles.description: Just east of Port Angeles, Dungeness Spit stretches over 5 miles into the Strait of Juan de Fuca, making it one of the longest natural sand spits in the world. It's a haven for over 250 species of birds, harbor seals, and countless tide pool creatures. The gentle walk along the spit offers stunning views of the Olympics and Vancouver Island.

puzzle_1.question: A gray whale can hold its breath for up to ___ minutes while diving for food.
puzzle_1.correct_response: That's exactly right, Barbara! Gray whales are remarkable divers.
puzzle_1.close_response: Very close! Gray whales can actually hold their breath for about 15 minutes.
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Gray whales can hold their breath for about 15 minutes — that's a long time underwater!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Gray whales migrate past Port Angeles every year, traveling between Alaska and Mexico — one of the longest migrations of any mammal on Earth, covering up to 12,000 miles round trip.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful, Ildiko! Pillangó is such a beautiful word for such a beautiful creature.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — such a lovely, musical word!
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is part of the Finno-Ugric language family, making it quite different from most European languages. Many Hungarian words have a poetic quality, like 'pillangó' which almost sounds like the flutter of butterfly wings.

puzzle_3.question: What do gardeners call the practice of planting different crops together to help them grow better?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! Companion planting is a wonderful gardening technique — tomatoes and basil are famous garden friends!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: That's called companion planting! For example, marigolds planted near tomatoes can help keep pests away naturally.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Companion planting has been used for centuries — Native Americans traditionally grew corn, beans, and squash together in 'Three Sisters' gardens, where each plant helped the others thrive.
